contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned about inherited traits. Today: some traits actually come from the environment, not from parents!

Not every trait is inherited — some come from the environment an organism grows up in. Two seeds from the very same plant can grow very differently: one planted in rich soil with lots of sunlight might grow tall and healthy, while the other planted in poor soil with little light might grow short. A puppy raised with plenty of food usually grows bigger than a littermate raised without enough food, even though they share the same parents. Explain in your own words why two seeds from the same plant might grow to different heights.
You just learned that the environment can shape traits too, not just inheritance! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Distinguish an environment-influenced trait from an inherited trait
Explain how sunlight/soil/food availability can affect an organism's growth
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's inherited-traits lesson.
2. Introduce environment-influenced traits using the seed/soil and puppy/food examples.
3. Have the child explain the different-height-seeds scenario in their own words.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: connect to a real memory — has the child ever seen two plants of the same type growing very differently?
Ready for more: ask the child to sort a list of traits (eye color, height from good nutrition, fur color, a scar from an injury) into inherited vs. environment-influenced
The seed/soil example is the clearest one for building genuine understanding of this distinction — spend extra time there
teacherGuide.answerKey: Seeds: the height difference comes from the environment (soil quality, sunlight amount), not inheritance, since both seeds came from the same plant. Fur color: usually inherited. Puppy size in this example: from the environment (food availability), since the puppies share the same parents but different food.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 3 Life Science standard 3-LS3-2: analyzing how the environment can affect an organism's traits, completing this week's traits pair before tomorrow's review.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question about environment-influenced traits.

rows.problem: Why might two seeds from the same plant grow to different heights?
Is fur color usually inherited, or from the environment?
Is a puppy's size (given enough or not enough food) inherited, or from the environment?
